_comment: Stage-1 recall eval, es-ES. Paraphrases, calibre/format discriminators and out-of-assortment negatives against the REAL catalogue (seed/catalogue.json — Cárnicas Aldonza). Every positive is written so it does NOT match a loaded alias (verified against matcher.normalize / strip_qty / strip_generic): the point is to measure dense+sparse+RERANK recall, which is the #1 risk — a SKU the retrieval misses can never be reranked back. Near-duplicate rows are included on purpose, but always with the discriminator the trade actually says («la sarta de medio kilo» vs «la sarta de un kilo entero»); a mention that genuinely cannot be resolved belongs in the DOUBT eval (tests/fixtures/golden_cases.json, bucket `doubt`), not here — recall has one right answer by definition. 65 positives = every sellable row in the catalogue; the three absent ones (pluma ibérica · chóped · queso de oveja) are in_assortment=false. Negatives = catalogue.json's five declared `_gaps` plus three obvious out-of-family asks; the matcher must abstain on all of them.
_rewritten: 2026-07-27 — the previous fixture was the ENGLISH pork list (sku-chops, sku-ribs-spare, sku-tenderloin…), every id of which the catalogue rewrite (08a2d18bb) deleted, so recall@k measured 0 against rows that no longer exist. Two of its five negatives («chicken breast fillets», «beef mince») are now things this house SELLS (PECHUGA POLLO FILETEADA · CALLOS TERNERA LIMPIOS), so the file was asserting the opposite of the truth. ⚠️ THE BAR in tests/recall_eval.py (recall@5 .95 / recall@1 .85 / neg_abstain .80) was calibrated on the OLD catalogue and has NOT been re-baselined against this one — the first real run on the box is a MEASUREMENT, not a verdict.
